title: Bifrost Configuration Schema
description: Schema for Bifrost HTTP transport configuration

$schema.description: Schema location for IDE validation. Defaults to "https://www.getbifrost.ai/schema" and can be set to a mirrored URL, file:// URL, or filesystem path for isolated deployments.

read_buffer_size.description: Read buffer size in bytes. This controls the size of the buffer used for reading HTTP headers.

base_path.description: URL path prefix Bifrost is served under behind a reverse proxy, e.g. "/bifrost" for https://abc.com/bifrost. Requests are accepted with or without the prefix, so proxies that strip it work too. The UI, redirects, and OAuth callback URLs use the prefix. Segments may not be "." or "..", and surrounding whitespace is not allowed. The first segment must not match a Bifrost route (such as api, v1, or openai) or a top-level UI path (such as assets or images). Overridden by the -base-path flag or BIFROST_BASE_PATH env var. Deploy-time only. Empty (default) serves at the domain root.

body_buffer_pool_limit_bytes.description: Largest request-body buffer (in bytes) a pooled keep-alive connection keeps for reuse between requests. Larger buffers are released after each request so connections do not pin their largest-ever body in memory; larger bodies are still accepted up to the max request body size. Not set uses the default (4 MiB); 0 means unlimited and keeps every buffer. Process-wide: also applies to outbound fasthttp request buffers. Deploy-time only.

plugin_download_private_allowlist.description: Hostnames, IP addresses, or CIDR ranges that custom plugin (.so) downloads are allowed to reach even when they resolve to a private/loopback/link-local/CGNAT address (blocked by default to prevent SSRF). Use only for trusted internal artifact hosts. Deploy-time only - read from config.json/environment at startup, never settable via the plugin admin API.

version.description: Controls how empty arrays in the allow-list fields of provider keys (models) and virtual keys (allowed_models, key_ids, tools_to_execute) are interpreted. Omit or set to 2 for v1.5.0+ semantics: empty = deny all, ["*"] = allow all. Set to 1 to restore v1.4.x semantics: empty = allow all. Projects under governance.projects are not affected: their allow-lists always treat empty or omitted as granting nothing, whatever this is set to.

source_of_truth.description: Controls how config.json is reconciled with the config store. "split" preserves existing merge behavior. "config.json" makes present config.json sections authoritative during startup sync; missing sections leave database rows untouched.

encryption_key.description: You can set the value as env.<ENV_VAR_NAME> to use an environment variable. We also read encryption key from BIFROST_ENCRYPTION_KEY environment variable. Note: once set, the encryption key cannot be changed unless you clean up the database. Accepts any string; a secure 32-byte AES-256 key will be derived using Argon2id KDF. If not provided, data will be saved in plain text. Recommended: use a passphrase of at least 16 bytes for better security

env_label.description: Short label (max 10 characters) displayed in the management UI sidebar to identify the environment (e.g. "staging", "prod"). Overrides the BIFROST_ENV_LABEL environment variable when both are set.

disable_onboarding.description: Hides the management UI setup checklist for every user. Unlike the in-app "hide for everyone" action, this is read from config.json on every start and never written to the config store, so it stays in effect on stateless deployments (ephemeral container storage, provider-less log viewers). Overrides the BIFROST_DISABLE_ONBOARDING environment variable when both are set.

setup_token.description: Operator-provisioned bootstrap secret required to create the very first admin account when no admin account is configured yet. In OSS, while dashboard auth is not active (no admin account, or auth disabled), every /api call must carry this value in the X-Bifrost-Setup-Token header. You can set the value as env.<ENV_VAR_NAME> to use an environment variable, or as vault.<path> to use a Vault secret reference. We also read the setup token from the BIFROST_SETUP_TOKEN environment variable. Identical across every node in a multi-node deployment (unlike a randomly generated value), so any node can authorize first-admin creation. Never persisted and never logged; if left unset, creating the first admin account is rejected until this is configured. Whitespace-only values are rejected.

drop_excess_requests.description: Whether to drop excess requests when pool is full

initial_pool_size.description: Initial size of the connection pool

prometheus_labels.description: Labels to use for Prometheus metrics

allowed_origins.description: CORS allowed origins: exact URI strings, wildcard-host patterns such as https://*.example.com, or "*". While dashboard auth is disabled, browser requests to the management API are accepted only from localhost origins, the gateway's own origin, and origins listed here explicitly; the "*" entry does not admit them.

disable_content_logging.description: Disable logging of sensitive content (inputs, outputs, embeddings, etc.)

retain_content_in_object_storage.description: When content logging is disabled, offload the full content to object storage as hidden instead of dropping it. Hidden content is never served back through the API/UI — the database row stays metadata-only and is only readable with direct access to the storage bucket. Requires object storage to be configured on the logs store.

allow_per_request_content_storage_overri.description: Allow individual requests to override content storage via the x-bf-disable-content-logging header or context key, and to opt in to raw-byte persistence in logs via x-bf-store-raw-request-response. When false (default), the global disable_content_logging setting is authoritative and per-request storage overrides are ignored. Does not control sending raw bytes back to callers — see allow_per_request_raw_override.

allow_per_request_raw_override.description: Allow individual requests to send raw provider request/response bytes back to the caller via the x-bf-send-back-raw-request and x-bf-send-back-raw-response headers. When false (default), the provider-level send_back_raw_request/response settings are authoritative and per-request overrides are ignored. Does not affect raw-byte persistence in logs — see allow_per_request_content_storage_override.

disable_db_pings_in_health.description: Disable DB pings in health check

dump_errors_in_console_logs.description: Dump full error details to the server console logs. Useful for debugging; may be noisy in production.

log_retention_days.description: Number of days to retain logs

enforce_auth_on_inference.description: Require auth (VK, API key, or user token) on inference endpoints. Defaults to true on new deployments and when creating the first enabled admin account if omitted; explicit false opts out. Existing deployments retain their stored setting when omitted.

dual_credential_conflict_behavior.description: Controls behavior when an inference request carries both an IDP access token (Authorization: Bearer <jwt>) and a virtual key (x-bf-vk header). 'error' rejects with 400. 'prefer_vk' drops the IDP token and authenticates via the VK. 'prefer_idp' (default) uses the IDP token for identity.

extra_fields_placement.description: Where inference responses carry Bifrost's extra_fields metadata. 'body' (default) keeps the extra_fields object in the JSON body. 'headers' removes extra_fields from the body (and from every streaming chunk) and sends its scalar fields as x-bifrost-* response headers. In 'headers' mode the large and nested fields are dropped and not sent anywhere: raw_request, raw_response, routing_metadata, guardrail_debug, parse_errors, and on errors key_statuses and billed_usage. Streaming responses only carry the fields known before the first chunk (routing identity, fallback index, cache lookup); per-chunk latency, chunk_index and final totals are dropped.

max_request_body_size_mb.description: Maximum request body size in MB. Also the ceiling for what a compressed request body may decompress to: within it a body may expand to at most 100 times its compressed size (1 MiB floor), and at most four times this cap of decompressed request bytes are held in flight at once

compat.description: Compat plugin configuration for request type conversion, parameter dropping, and parameter value conversion

convert_text_to_chat.description: Convert text completion requests to chat for models that only support chat

convert_chat_to_responses.description: Convert chat completion requests to responses for models that only support responses

should_drop_params.description: Drop unsupported parameters based on model catalog allowlist

should_convert_params.description: Converts model parameter values that are not supported by the model.

azure_deepseek.description: Convert Azure DeepSeek responses requests to chat completions so reasoning is preserved for coding harnesses.

force_reasoning_only_models_to_responses.description: Convert chat completion requests to responses for models whose datasheet sets supports_reasoning_with_tool_calls to false, so reasoning is kept instead of being forced off.

convert_decision_to_responses.description: Emulate decision requests through the model's Responses API (a forced function tool) when the provider does not serve the model on a native decisions endpoint. Off by default: without it, such requests fail with unsupported_operation.

header_filter_config.description: Global header filtering configuration for x-bf-eh-* headers forwarded to LLM providers

allowlist.description: If non-empty, only these headers (from x-bf-eh-* prefix) are allowed to be forwarded

denylist.description: Headers to always block from being forwarded

async_job_result_ttl.description: Default TTL for async job results in seconds (default: 3600 = 1 hour)

required_headers.description: Headers that must be present on every request. Requests missing any of these headers are rejected with 400. Case-insensitive matching.

logging_headers.description: Headers to capture in log metadata. Values are extracted from incoming requests and stored in the metadata field of log entries.

whitelisted_routes.description: Routes that bypass auth middleware. Requests to these exact paths skip authentication checks.

hide_deleted_virtual_keys_in_filters.description: When true, deleted virtual keys are omitted from logs filter data.

hidden_request_types.description: Request types excluded from dashboard and log API reads. Logs are still stored; an empty array shows all request types. Editable from the UI under Logs Settings.

usage_estimation_tokenizers.description: Embedded tokenizer vocabularies used to estimate the usage of a cancelled or timed-out stream whose provider never reported it. An empty array counts every model with o200k_base or cl100k_base. Each listed family preloads in the background at startup and keeps 4-18 MB in memory; "all" enables every family.

allowed_headers.description: Additional allowed headers for CORS and WebSocket

allow_direct_keys.description: Allow callers to bypass the registered key pool by supplying x-bf-direct-key: true and the provider's raw API key in an Authorization (Bearer), x-api-key, or x-goog-api-key header.

delete_expired_virtual_keys.description: Delete expired virtual keys automatically. A daily cleanup job removes every key whose expiry has passed unless the key sets delete_after_expire to false; keys with delete_after_expire true are removed regardless.

enforce_vk_object_ownership.description: Restrict provider objects (files, batches, videos, containers, container files, cached contents and live sessions) to the virtual key that created them. Another virtual key gets 404 for them and does not see them in list responses. Requests without a virtual key are not restricted. Creators are recorded even while this is off, so turning it back on also covers objects created meanwhile; an object whose creator could not be recorded stays reachable to every virtual key.

skip_access_profile_user_virtual_key_cre.description: Enterprise only. When true, a user's first access profile never creates a virtual key for them. Keys the user already owns are still governed by the profile while they hold one.

skip_access_profile_user_virtual_key_del.description: Enterprise only. When true, removing a user's last access profile never deletes their virtual keys; they are kept as ordinary keys with none of the profile's providers or access. Deleting the user still deletes their keys.

entity_access_profile_mode.description: Enterprise only. How the access profiles of the teams, business units and customers a caller belongs to combine with the caller's own access. Takes the same values as a project's access_rule. 'union' (default) lets each of them add to what the caller may reach. 'intersect' makes each level that holds an active profile cap it instead: the caller keeps only what their own profiles (or virtual key) allow AND what at least one of their team or business unit profiles allows AND what at least one of their customer profiles allows. A level holding no active profile is skipped. The cap covers providers, models, provider keys; agents are not capped, since team, business unit and customer profiles cannot grant them. Budgets and rate limits are charged as in 'union' mode. The x-bf-customer-id / x-bf-customer-name scope headers are ignored in 'intersect' mode.

vk_rotation_cooldown.description: Cooldown after virtual key rotation: grace period during which the previous key value still authenticates. Accepts a Go duration string (e.g. "5m", "1h"); integer values are nanoseconds (Go duration JSON encoding), so prefer strings. 0 or an empty string disables the grace period (the old value stops working immediately). Maximum 30 days (2592000000000000 ns); string durations are bounds-checked at runtime.

routing_chain_max_depth.description: Maximum depth for routing rule chain evaluation

skills_external_client_url.description: Public base URL for Skills Repository marketplaces. Required to enable Claude Code and Codex marketplace serving; skill management and downloads remain available when unset. Supports env var and vault references.

governance.description: Governance configuration for budgets, rate limits, customers, teams, virtual keys, and routing rules

reset_config.description: Window settings the reset duration cannot express. Only valid when reset_duration is quarterly ('1Q').

quarter_start_month.description: First month of Q1 as 1-12, so a fiscal year opening in April (4) gives Apr-Jun / Jul-Sep / Oct-Dec / Jan-Mar. Omitted or 0 means January. Quarter boundaries repeat every three months, so only the value modulo 3 changes the reset dates: January, April, July and October all reset on calendar quarters and differ only in which quarter is labelled Q1.

current_usage.description: Seed value only: current usage in dollars, applied when the budget is first created. Runtime-owned thereafter - the value here is ignored on every subsequent sync so a config.json reload cannot overwrite live accounting.

last_reset.description: Seed value only: last time the budget was reset, applied when the budget is first created. Runtime-owned thereafter, like current_usage.

virtual_key_id.description: ID of the virtual key this budget belongs to (mutually exclusive with provider_config_id)

provider_config_id.description: ID of the provider config this budget belongs to (mutually exclusive with virtual_key_id)

model_config_id.description: ID of the model config this budget belongs to (mutually exclusive with the other owner IDs)

customer_id.description: ID of the customer this budget belongs to (mutually exclusive with the other owner IDs)

team_id.description: ID of the team this budget belongs to (mutually exclusive with virtual_key_id and provider_config_id)

calendar_aligned.description: Deprecated: set calendar_aligned on the owner (team / virtual key / access profile) instead. Kept for backward compatibility with older config.json files; ignored unless a reconciler promotes it to its owner.

override_amount.description: Amount added to max_limit while an override is active

override_mode.description: How long the override stays active: 'cycles' for a finite number of reset windows, 'forever' until explicitly removed, '' for no override

override_cycles_remaining.description: Reset windows the current override still covers, including the current one. Derived state: recomputed from override_anchor_reset, override_cycles_total and last_reset, so it is never the source of truth.

override_cycles_total.description: Number of reset windows the current finite override was granted for. Immutable for the life of a grant.

override_anchor_reset.description: Window boundary at which the current finite override was granted. Immutable for the life of a grant; absent when there is no finite override.

token_current_usage.description: Seed value only: current token usage, applied when the rate limit is first created. Runtime-owned thereafter - the value here is ignored on every subsequent sync so a config.json reload cannot overwrite live counters.

token_last_reset.description: Seed value only: last time the token counter was reset, applied when the rate limit is first created. Runtime-owned thereafter, like token_current_usage.

request_current_usage.description: Seed value only: current request usage, applied when the rate limit is first created. Runtime-owned thereafter - the value here is ignored on every subsequent sync so a config.json reload cannot overwrite live counters.

request_last_reset.description: Seed value only: last time the request counter was reset, applied when the rate limit is first created. Runtime-owned thereafter, like request_current_usage.

calendar_aligned.description: Deprecated: set calendar_aligned on the owner (team / virtual key / access profile) instead. Kept for backward compatibility with older config.json files; ignored unless a reconciler promotes it to its owner.

budgets.description: Inline budget configurations for this customer. Each entry must have a unique reset_duration. Mutually exclusive with budget_id.

budget_id.description: Single budget reference (pre-declared in governance.budgets). Deprecated in favour of inline budgets.

access_profile.description: Name of the access profile (defined in access_profiles) this customer holds. The profile governs everything under the customer and replaces its own budgets and rate limit, so it cannot be combined with them. Under source_of_truth "split" the declaration is applied when it is new or changed and dashboard changes are kept otherwise; under "config.json" it is enforced on every startup and an entry without access_profile has its profile removed.

calendar_aligned.description: Snap the customer's budget and rate-limit reset windows to clean calendar boundaries (day, week, month, year)

virtual_key_count.description: Computed count of virtual keys associated with this customer

source_id.description: Optional external source identifier (e.g. SCIM group ID) used to map this team to an upstream system. Unique when set.

access_profile.description: Name of the access profile (defined in access_profiles) this team holds. The profile governs everything under the team and replaces its own budgets and rate limit, so it cannot be combined with them. Under source_of_truth "split" the declaration is applied when it is new or changed and dashboard changes are kept otherwise; under "config.json" it is enforced on every startup and an entry without access_profile has its profile removed.

calendar_aligned.description: Snap the team's budget and rate-limit reset windows to clean calendar boundaries (day, week, month, year)

virtual_key_count.description: Computed count of virtual keys associated with this team

business_units.description: Business unit configurations with optional team assignments

budgets.description: Inline budget configurations for this business unit, matched by id. One budget per reset_duration is recommended. Only the business unit's own calendar_aligned is read; calendar_aligned on an entry is ignored.

budget_id.description: Deprecated: use budgets. ID of a budget declared in governance.budgets that this business unit holds, alongside any inline budgets.

calendar_aligned.description: When true, the business unit's budgets and rate limit reset at calendar boundaries (start of hour, day, week, month, quarter or year) instead of rolling windows.

access_profile.description: Name of the access profile (defined in access_profiles) this business unit holds. The profile governs everything under the business unit and replaces its own budgets and rate limit, so it cannot be combined with them. Under source_of_truth "split" the declaration is applied when it is new or changed and dashboard changes are kept otherwise; under "config.json" it is enforced on every startup and an entry without access_profile has its profile removed.

team_ids.description: Team IDs to assign to this business unit

roles.description: RBAC role definitions. Roles are created or updated on startup if the config hash changes; system roles and dashboard-created roles are never deleted.

dac.description: Data Access Control scope: own-data (user's own records), team-data (plus records of the user's teams), business-unit-data (plus records of the user's business units), customer-data (everything under the customers the user reaches through their teams or business units), all-data (unrestricted). Defaults to all-data.

entity_dac.description: Per-entity Data Access Control overrides, keyed by resource name. Each entry narrows or widens the role's global dac for that one entity; entities not listed follow dac. Resources accepting an override as of this release: Logs, AuditLogs, VirtualKeys, Users, Teams, Customers, BusinessUnits, RBAC, APIKeys, AccessProfiles, RoutingRules, GuardrailsConfig, Projects.

access_profile.description: Name of the access profile (defined in access_profiles) to attach as the default for this role. Changing this field triggers a re-sync on next startup. Leave unset to let the dashboard manage the assignment.

access_profiles.description: Names of all access profiles granted by this role. When present, this field takes precedence over access_profile; an empty list removes all profile grants.

permissions.description: List of resource+operation permission pairs to grant to this role

resource.description: Permission resource (e.g. Logs, VirtualKeys, Users, ModelProvider, Metrics, Guardrails, AccessProfiles, Roles, BusinessUnits, AuditLogs, Billing)

operation.description: Permission operation (e.g. View, Create, Update, Delete, Download, RunInference, ManageInference, ViewInference)

projects.description: Projects: per-request access gates and accounting scopes that requests opt into. Matched by name and created or updated on startup when the config hash changes; membership is managed from the dashboard and is never declared here.

value.description: The virtual key value. A literal, or an "env.VAR"/"vault.path" reference resolved to plaintext at load time.

is_active.description: Whether the virtual key is active

expires_at.description: Optional expiry timestamp (RFC3339). Once passed, requests using this virtual key are rejected. Omit for a key that never expires.

delete_after_expire.description: Delete this virtual key automatically once expires_at has passed. A daily cleanup job removes it and posts a notification. Omit to follow client.delete_expired_virtual_keys; true or false override it for this key. Requires expires_at.

calendar_aligned.description: Snap all budget resets to calendar boundaries (day, week, month, year)

allow_all_providers.description: Grant this virtual key access to every provider, including ones added later. Coexists with provider_configs: a provider that also has a config row still has that config's model allow/blacklist, budgets, rate limits, and key selection applied; providers without a config get all models, all keys, and no per-provider limits. When false (default), access is deny-by-default via provider_configs.

disable_content_logging.description: Per-key override of client.disable_content_logging for requests made with this virtual key. Omit to inherit the client setting. true keeps request and response content out of the log store and out of OpenTelemetry export for this key's traffic; other observability connectors follow their own disable_content_logging until they adopt the trace mark. When content logging ends up disabled for a request, the log row is still written without content; with client.retain_content_in_object_storage on and an object-storage-backed log store, the full payload is then kept there as hidden content that the API and UI never serve. false forces content into the log store even when the client setting is true; observability connectors keep following their own disable_content_logging. The x-bf-disable-content-logging request header, when client.allow_per_request_content_storage_override is on, still takes precedence over this value for the log store.

metadata.description: Custom key/value metadata for this virtual key (for example cost_center, project, owner, environment). Copied onto every log entry the key produces, so logs and spend can be filtered by it; on a key collision it overrides request-supplied log metadata (x-bf-lh-* headers, configured logging headers, x-bf-dim-* dimensions). Keys may contain letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-' (max 256 characters) and may not be system-reserved (isAsyncRequest, bifrost_alb_*); values are strings of at most 512 characters; at most 50 entries.

team_id.description: Associated team ID (mutually exclusive with customer_id and business_unit_id)

customer_id.description: Associated customer ID (mutually exclusive with team_id and business_unit_id)

business_unit_id.description: Associated business unit ID (mutually exclusive with team_id and customer_id)

access_profile_id.description: Deprecated and ignored: direct access-profile assignment was reverted in v1.5.9 (#3669/#3670) and the column dropped. Accepted only for backward-compatible validation of older config files.

is_access_profile_managed.description: Read-only, server-computed flag: true when the virtual key is governed by an access profile. Never persisted and ignored if set in config.json.

assigned_user.description: Read-only, server-populated projection of the user this virtual key is assigned to. Present as an object (or null when resolved but unassigned) on governance read paths; omitted when the assignee could not be resolved. Never persisted and ignored if set in config.json.

provider_configs.description: Provider configurations for this virtual key (empty means no providers allowed, deny-by-default)

allOf.$comment: A virtual key belongs to at most one owner: team_id and customer_id cannot both name one.
A virtual key belongs to at most one owner: team_id and business_unit_id cannot both name one.
A virtual key belongs to at most one owner: customer_id and business_unit_id cannot both name one.

routing_rules.description: Routing rules for dynamic provider/model selection based on CEL expressions

pricing_overrides.description: Scoped pricing overrides applied at runtime by the model catalog

model_configs.description: Per-model rate limit and budget configurations

model_name.description: Model name to apply the configuration to

provider.description: Optional provider name to scope this config

scope.description: Scope where this config applies: "global" (default) or "virtual_key"

scope_id.description: Target entity ID for non-global scopes (e.g. virtual key ID). Required when scope != "global"

calendar_aligned.description: Snap this config's budget resets to calendar boundaries (e.g. a monthly budget resets on the 1st) rather than rolling windows. For virtual_key-scoped configs it inherits the virtual key's setting.

budget_id.description: Deprecated — single budget reference. Use budget_ids instead.

budget_ids.description: List of budget IDs (from governance.budgets) to associate with this model config. Supports multiple budgets (e.g. daily + monthly). Replaces budget_id.

rate_limit_id.description: Rate limit ID to associate with this model

store_raw_request_response.description: Capture raw request/response for internal logging only; strip from API responses returned to clients (default: false)

ignore_provider_cost.description: Ignore the provider-reported usage.cost and calculate cost from Bifrost's model pricing and pricing overrides (default: false)

datasheet_overrides.description: Edits to the synced model datasheet (pricing and model parameters) that survive every datasheet sync. Matched by (provider, model, mode) with hash-based change detection: a file entry is applied when it changes, so edits made in the UI stand until the file entry itself changes. In config.json source-of-truth mode stored overrides absent from this list are removed.

model_routers.description: Named model routers, each a complexity classifier with its own phrases and settings, the model each tier gets, and the requests it takes after the routing rules. They are separate from governance.complexity_analyzer_config, which routing rules read complexity_tier from. Unless config.json is the source of truth, dashboard edits to sections the file has not changed are kept.

type.description: Vector store type (use "redis" for Redis or Valkey-compatible endpoints). "chromem" runs in-process rather than against a service, so its data is local to one node and is not shared between replicas

config.description: Backend-specific settings. The block must match the backend named by the sibling "type"; the conditionals below pin it to that backend rather than accepting any backend's shape

password.description: Database password. Use password_command instead when the password must be generated dynamically.

password_command.description: Command executed without a shell to produce the database password on stdout for each new physical connection.

command.description: Executable path or name to run

args.description: Arguments passed directly to the executable

timeout.description: Command timeout as a Go duration string (default: 10s)

cache_ttl.description: How long a resolved password is reused across new physical connections (Go duration string, default 60s). Without caching the command runs on every new connection. Keep this below the credential's validity window: a rotation shorter than the TTL will fail connections until the cached value expires.

max_idle_conns.description: Maximum number of idle connections in the pool (default: 5)

max_open_conns.description: Maximum number of open connections to the database (default: 50)

conn_max_lifetime.description: Maximum lifetime for physical database connections as a Go duration string

conn_max_idle_time.description: How long an idle physical connection is kept before being closed (Go duration string, default 5m). Without this the idle cap alone controls pool size, so bursts above max_idle_conns close and reopen connections repeatedly. Note the logs store and config store open separate pools, so a pod's connection ceiling is the sum of their max_open_conns.

statement_timeout.description: Server-side statement_timeout set on every runtime pool connection (Go duration string, default 120s). Bounds a runaway query so it cannot hold a pooled connection and its locks indefinitely. "0" or a negative value leaves the server default. Migrations and background index builds are never bound by it.

idle_in_transaction_session_timeout.description: Server-side idle_in_transaction_session_timeout set on every runtime pool connection (Go duration string, default 120s). Ends a session left idle inside an open transaction, which would otherwise hold row locks and block vacuum. "0" or a negative value leaves the server default.

migration_lock_retry_budget.description: How long a schema migration step keeps retrying after lock timeouts before the process gives up and exits (Go duration string, default 10m). During a rolling upgrade a step that needs a table lock retries while older replicas' long queries hold the table; raise this on large deployments so the budget outlasts those queries, and keep the Kubernetes startup probe at least as long. Each lock timeout logs the sessions holding the table so an operator can cancel them instead of waiting.

password.description: Database password. Use password_command instead when the password must be generated dynamically.

password_command.description: Command executed without a shell to produce the database password on stdout for each new physical connection.

command.description: Executable path or name to run

args.description: Arguments passed directly to the executable

timeout.description: Command timeout as a Go duration string (default: 10s)

cache_ttl.description: How long a resolved password is reused across new physical connections (Go duration string, default 60s). Without caching the command runs on every new connection. Keep this below the credential's validity window: a rotation shorter than the TTL will fail connections until the cached value expires.

max_idle_conns.description: Maximum number of idle connections in the pool (default: 5)

max_open_conns.description: Maximum number of open connections to the database (default: 50)

matview_refresh_interval.description: How often to refresh dashboard materialized views. Go duration string (e.g. '1m', '5m', '1h'). Default 1m. Raise this when matview refresh CPU cost is material on the database instance. Positive values below 5s are clamped up to 5s. Set 'off' or a zero duration (e.g. '0s') to disable materialized-view maintenance entirely; dashboard queries fall back to the raw tables.

matview_refresh_timeout.description: Maximum time for a single materialized view refresh pass. Go duration string, min 30s, max 30m. Unset derives a budget from matview_refresh_interval (5x the interval, at least 5m). A refresh holds a pooled connection and a session advisory lock across every view, so without a bound one stuck refresh leaves the views permanently stale across all replicas.

matview_refresh_temp_file_limit.description: Caps the temp files each Postgres process running a materialized view statement may write (Postgres temp_file_limit, e.g. '10GB'; parallel workers each get the cap). A refresh over a very large logs table can spill tens of GB, and a full disk fails every query on the server. A statement that hits the cap fails and the view keeps its previous contents. Unset leaves the server setting alone. The database role needs superuser or GRANT SET ON PARAMETER temp_file_limit; without it the cap is skipped with a warning.

migration_matview_cancel_after.description: How long schema migrations wait for an in-flight materialized view refresh pass (from any replica, including older releases during a rolling upgrade) before cancelling its REFRESH statements. Migrations pause refreshes for their whole run, because a long refresh on a large logs table blocks their CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY and ALTER TABLE logs statements. A cancelled concurrent refresh rolls back and the view keeps its previous contents. Go duration string; unset uses 60s; "off" never cancels and only waits.

conn_max_lifetime.description: Maximum lifetime for physical database connections as a Go duration string

conn_max_idle_time.description: How long an idle physical connection is kept before being closed (Go duration string, default 5m). Without this the idle cap alone controls pool size, so bursts above max_idle_conns close and reopen connections repeatedly. Note the logs store and config store open separate pools, so a pod's connection ceiling is the sum of their max_open_conns.

statement_timeout.description: Server-side statement_timeout set on every runtime pool connection (Go duration string, default 120s). Bounds a runaway query so it cannot hold a pooled connection and its locks indefinitely. "0" or a negative value leaves the server default. Migrations and background index builds are never bound by it.

idle_in_transaction_session_timeout.description: Server-side idle_in_transaction_session_timeout set on every runtime pool connection (Go duration string, default 120s). Ends a session left idle inside an open transaction, which would otherwise hold row locks and block vacuum. "0" or a negative value leaves the server default.

migration_lock_retry_budget.description: How long a schema migration step keeps retrying after lock timeouts before the process gives up and exits (Go duration string, default 10m). During a rolling upgrade a step that needs a table lock retries while older replicas' long queries hold the table; raise this on large deployments so the budget outlasts those queries, and keep the Kubernetes startup probe at least as long. Each lock timeout logs the sessions holding the table so an operator can cancel them instead of waiting.

port.description: ClickHouse port. Defaults by protocol: native 9000 (9440 TLS), http 8123 (8443 TLS)

secure.description: Enable TLS (native: secure=true; http: switches to https)

max_query_size.description: ClickHouse max_query_size setting in bytes, the longest SQL text the server will parse (default: 16777216)

cluster.description: Optional cluster name; when set, DDL runs ON CLUSTER with replicated table engines

writer.description: Async logging writer queue and batch tuning. Omitted fields use runtime defaults.

max_batch_size.description: Maximum number of log entries to batch before flushing (default: 1000)

batch_interval.description: Maximum time to wait before flushing a partial batch as a Go duration string (default: 5s)

max_batch_bytes.description: Approximate byte-size ceiling for a batch before flushing (default: 314572800)

write_queue_capacity.description: Buffered queue capacity for pending log writes (default: 10000). This queue is also the buffer while the writer pauses for another node's log store migration, so it bounds how much of that window is absorbed without drops.

deferred_usage_concurrency.description: Maximum concurrent deferred usage database updates (default: 5)

object_storage.description: Optional object storage for offloading LLM log payloads. When configured, full payloads are stored in S3/GCS/Azure Blob while the DB keeps lightweight index data.

bucket.description: Bucket name, or Azure Blob container name. Supports env var reference (e.g. env.S3_BUCKET) or a structured secret reference.

prefix.description: Key prefix for stored objects (default: bifrost)

compress.description: Legacy gzip switch, equivalent to compression "gzip". An explicit compression value takes precedence. Default: false

format.description: Encoding of offloaded log payload objects. json writes {id}.json.gz objects; parquet writes single-row {id}.parquet files (one UTF8 column per payload field) readable by Athena, Spark and DuckDB. Objects written before a format change stay readable. parquet is supported on s3 and azure. Default: json

compression.description: Compression for offloaded log payload objects. For json it is applied to the whole object (none or gzip only). For parquet it is the page codec inside the file (none, gzip, snappy or zstd), and no outer gzip is added. Default: none for json (gzip when compress is true), snappy for parquet.

region.description: AWS region. Supports env var reference

endpoint.description: Custom S3-compatible endpoint for MinIO/R2. Supports env var reference

access_key_id.description: AWS access key ID. Omit to use default credential chain (instance role, env vars, etc.). Supports env var reference

secret_access_key.description: AWS secret access key. Supports env var reference

session_token.description: AWS session token for STS temporary credentials. Supports env var reference

role_arn.description: AWS IAM role ARN for STS AssumeRole. Works with static creds or instance role. Supports env var reference

force_path_style.description: Use path-style URLs for S3 (required for MinIO). Default: false

credentials_json.description: GCP service account credentials JSON or file path. Omit to use Application Default Credentials. Supports env var reference

credentials.description: Deprecated: use credentials_json. Kept for backwards compatibility.

project_id.description: GCP project ID override. Supports env var reference

format.description: parquet is not supported for gcs yet

object_storage_exclude_request_types.description: Request types (log object type, e.g. list_models, embedding) whose logs are not offloaded to object storage. These logs are written to the logs database in full instead. Hidden logs (content logging disabled with client.retain_content_in_object_storage on) are still offloaded, so their content never lands in the database.

object_storage_exclude_fields.description: LLM log payload field DB column names that should NOT be offloaded to object storage and must remain in the database (e.g. output_message, input_history, raw_request, raw_response). Unknown names are ignored. error_details always remains in the database (except on content-hidden logs), since the error type, error code and status code breakdowns query it; any raw provider bodies inside it are offloaded unless error_details is listed here.

retention_days.description: Days to retain log entries. 0 disables retention-based cleanup.

capture_client_ip.description: Record the caller's IP as client_ip on LLM logs, in the order enterprise audit logs use: leftmost X-Forwarded-For, else X-Real-IP, else the TCP peer. The headers are caller-supplied and not verified; to trust the value, run behind a proxy that overwrites them and block direct access to Bifrost. Off by default. When off, new logs leave client_ip empty in the logs database and in object storage; turning it off does not clear values already recorded. Takes effect on restart.

skills_registry.description: Declarative Skills Repository definitions reconciled from config.json

enabled.description: Whether config-defined skills should be reconciled at startup

skills.description: Skills to create or update from config.json

name.description: Name of the plugin (built-in: telemetry, prompts, logging, governance, semantic_cache, otel, or custom plugin name)

path.description: Path to the plugin (optional, required for dynamic plugins)

placement.description: DB-Backed Only. Whether this plugin runs before, after, or as a built-in. Default: post_builtin. Setting or changing it here reloads the plugin entry from config.json; omit it and the stored value is kept.

order.description: DB-Backed Only. Position within placement group. Lower values execute earlier. Default: 0. Setting or changing it here reloads the plugin entry from config.json; omit it and the stored value is kept.

semaphore_size.description: For plugins that implement ObservabilityPlugin (receive completed traces): cap on how many traces may be injected into this plugin concurrently. A saturated cap causes new traces to be dropped for this plugin only, not process-wide. Ignored by plugins that don't receive traces (default: 10000).

inject_timeout.description: For plugins that implement ObservabilityPlugin: timeout for a single Inject call from the tracer, as a Go duration string (default: 5s). Bounds how long a hung connector can hold a concurrency-budget slot. Ignored by plugins that don't receive traces.

config.description: Configuration for the telemetry plugin (Prometheus metrics)

custom_labels.description: Custom labels to add to Prometheus metrics

metrics_enabled.description: Serve the /metrics scrape endpoint. Defaults to true when omitted.

overhead_breakdown_enabled.description: Export the per-component overhead histogram bifrost_overhead_component_microseconds (overhead latency split by the overhead_component label). Off by default. Requires tracing to be active, since the breakdown is computed from completed trace spans.

user_labels_enabled.description: Add user_id and user_name labels to every bifrost_* metric. Off by default: these are unbounded, so they multiply metric series by end-user count on top of a virtual_key_id label that already reaches tens of thousands of values in large deployments. Prometheus holds every label combination in memory for the retention period and cannot drop a label afterwards. Per-user attribution is available without this from the user attributes on OTEL spans.

push_gateway.description: Configuration for pushing metrics to a Prometheus Push Gateway for multi-node cluster deployments

enabled.description: Whether to enable pushing metrics to the Push Gateway

push_gateway_url.description: URL of the Prometheus Push Gateway (e.g., http://pushgateway:9091)

instance_id.description: Instance identifier for grouping metrics. If not set, hostname is used automatically.

push_interval.description: How often to push metrics in seconds

basic_auth.description: Basic authentication credentials for the Push Gateway

disable_content_logging.description: Disable logging of request and response content

retain_content_in_object_storage.description: When content logging is disabled, offload the full content to object storage as hidden instead of dropping it. Hidden content is never served back through the API/UI. Requires object storage to be configured on the logs store.

allow_per_request_content_storage_overri.description: Allow individual requests to override content storage via the x-bf-disable-content-logging header or context key, and to opt in to raw-byte persistence in logs via x-bf-store-raw-request-response. When false (default), per-request storage overrides are ignored. Does not control sending raw bytes back to callers — see allow_per_request_raw_override.

logging_headers.description: List of headers to capture in log metadata

is_vk_mandatory.description: Whether virtual key (x-bf-vk header) is mandatory for all requests

required_headers.description: List of headers that must be present in requests

config.description: Configuration for the semantic cache plugin

provider.description: Provider to use for generating embeddings. Required for semantic search; omit it for direct hash mode with dimension: 1.

embedding_model.description: Model to use for generating embeddings in provider-backed semantic caching. Required when provider is set and not allowed in direct-only mode.

ttl.description: Time-to-live for cached responses (supports duration strings like '5m', '1h' or seconds as number, default: 5min)

threshold.description: Cosine similarity threshold for semantic matching (default: 0.8)

dimension.description: Dimension for vector store embeddings. Use 1 for direct (hash-based) caching without an embedding provider.

default_cache_key.description: Default cache key used when no per-request key is provided. When set, all requests without an explicit x-bf-cache-key header will use this value and be cached automatically.

conversation_history_threshold.description: Skip caching for requests with more than this number of messages in conversation history (default: 3)

cache_by_model.description: Include model in cache key (default: true)

cache_by_provider.description: Include provider in cache key (default: true)

exclude_system_prompt.description: Exclude system prompt in cache key (default: false)

cache_tool_call_responses.description: Persist responses that carry tool calls (chat tool_calls or Responses API function_call/custom_tool_call/computer_call/local_shell_call/mcp_call/mcp_approval_request items). Off by default: a replayed tool call runs in a later caller's agent loop with arguments chosen for someone else's prompt.

disable_identity_scoping.description: Share cache entries across identities. Off by default: an entry is only served to the identity that wrote it, meaning the same virtual key and the same user, even when requests share a cache key or default_cache_key. Set to true to let every identity share entries by cache key.

config.description: Configuration for the OpenTelemetry plugin. Supports the legacy single-profile shape or the profiles wrapper for multiple collectors.

identity_source.description: Where a federated key gets the OIDC identity token it exchanges. Shared by every provider that supports workload identity federation.

type.description: file: read the token from path on every exchange, so a token the platform rotates on disk is picked up. inline: use token as given

path.description: Absolute path of the identity token, for type file (can use env. prefix). Must be under /var/run/secrets or /run/secrets, or a directory listed in the BIFROST_OIDC_ALLOWED_CREDENTIAL_DIRS environment variable

token.description: The identity token itself, for type inline (can use env. prefix)

datasheet_override.description: One datasheet entry edit. Both patches are RFC 7386 JSON merge patches: a key sets the value, null clears it, and an omitted key keeps the upstream value.

provider.description: Provider of the datasheet entry, e.g. openai

model.description: Model name as it appears in the datasheet

mode.description: Datasheet mode (chat, responses, embedding, ...). Omit to apply the pricing patch to every mode of the model. Required when is_custom is true.

is_custom.description: Adds an entry the upstream datasheet does not list, e.g. a fine-tuned or self-hosted model

pricing_patch.description: Merge patch over the pricing entry: context_length, max_input_tokens, max_output_tokens, is_deprecated, base_model, architecture and any cost field such as input_cost_per_token

params_patch.description: Merge patch over the model-parameters entry: supports_* capability flags, reasoning_effort_levels, max_output_tokens, supported_endpoints and other model parameters. provider cannot be patched.

azure_storage_secret.description: A nonempty literal, env.VAR_NAME reference, or structured secret reference.

azure_object_storage.description: Azure Blob Storage. Supply a connection string, or a Blob service endpoint to use DefaultAzureCredential (including workload identity). Authentication is independent of inference-provider credentials.

endpoint.description: Azure Blob service URL for DefaultAzureCredential authentication. Mutually exclusive with connection_string. Supports env var and structured secret references.

connection_string.description: Azure Storage connection string. Mutually exclusive with endpoint. Supports env var and structured secret references.

global_proxy_config.description: Global outbound proxy (the dashboard's proxy settings page) and which components use it. Under source_of_truth "split" it is applied when new or changed and dashboard edits are kept otherwise; under "config.json" it is applied on every startup. Omit to manage the proxy from the dashboard. Not the same as a provider's own proxy_config.

type.description: Proxy type: http (an http:// or https:// proxy URL) or socks5 (a socks5:// or socks5h:// proxy URL). A bare host:port takes its scheme from the type.

url.description: Proxy URL, e.g. http://proxy.example.com:8080 (supports env.VAR_NAME). Required when enabled.

no_proxy.description: Comma-separated hosts that bypass the proxy: exact hosts, .example.com (domain and subdomains), *.example.com (subdomains), or *

skip_tls_verify.description: Skip TLS certificate verification for the proxy

enable_for_scim.description: Enterprise: route SCIM directory sync and identity-provider requests through the proxy

enable_for_inference.description: Route inference requests through the proxy

enable_for_api.description: Route API requests through the proxy

definition.description: Replaces this tier's shipped definition. Omit to use the default.

signals.description: Replaces this tier's shipped signals. Omit to use the default.

examples.description: Replaces this tier's shipped examples. Omit to use the default.

plugin_span_filter.description: Controls which plugin hook spans this observability connector exports. Omit to export all plugin spans. Mode "include" exports only the listed plugins; mode "exclude" exports everything except them. Plugin names match the <name> in the span name "plugin.<name>.<stage>".

otel_profile_config.description: OpenTelemetry export profile. This legacy single-profile shape is still accepted directly as the plugin config.

enabled.description: Whether this profile exports traces and metrics

traces_enabled.description: Enable trace export for this profile. When false, no traces are sent and collector_url is not required, giving a metrics-only profile (pair with metrics_enabled).

service_name.description: Service name to be used for tracing

trace_type.description: Type of trace to use for the OTEL collector

protocol.description: Protocol to use for the OTEL collector

export_timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds for a single trace export. Bounds how long a slow or unreachable collector can hold an export goroutine; gRPC exports have no other timeout.

metrics_enabled.description: Enable push-based metrics export via OTLP. Recommended for multi-node cluster deployments.

metrics_endpoint.description: OTLP metrics endpoint URL (e.g., http://otel-collector:4318/v1/metrics for HTTP or otel-collector:4317 for gRPC)

overhead_breakdown_enabled.description: Export the per-component overhead histogram bifrost_overhead_component_microseconds (overhead latency split by the overhead_component attribute). Off by default. Requires metrics_enabled and an active trace, since the breakdown is computed from completed spans.

request_headers.description: Request header name patterns (exact or wildcard like x-custom-*) to capture and emit as span attributes. Note: * captures all headers including sensitive ones like Authorization.

disable_content_logging.description: When true, message content (input/output messages, embeddings, tool definitions, and tool call arguments/results) is dropped from exported spans. Only metadata such as model, tokens, and latency is sent to the collector.

excluded_attributes.description: Span attribute names to drop before export, matched exactly (e.g. "gen_ai.request.tools"). Unknown names are ignored.

export_raw_payloads.description: Attach the raw provider request/response bodies to LLM spans. Off by default: these carry provider-specific fields the normalized view does not. Guardrail redaction still applies. Also requires the provider's store_raw_request_response, and is suppressed by disable_content_logging. Bodies over 256 KB are dropped.

group_traces_by_session.description: When true, requests sharing the same x-bf-session-id header are grouped into a single OTEL trace, each request's root span appearing as a top-level sibling. An inbound W3C traceparent takes precedence, leaving that request on its own distributed trace.

disable_root_span_content.description: When true, input/output message content is dropped from the root span only; the underlying generation (llm.call) span retains the full content. This removes the duplicate input/output stored at the trace level (e.g. the Langfuse trace Input/Output goes empty) to reduce downstream storage.

apply_trace_dimensions_to_child_spans.description: When true, x-bf-dim-* request dimensions stored on the trace are merged onto child spans as well as the root. Span attributes win on conflict. The suffixes path and method, and keys in reserved attribute namespaces (gen_ai., llm., bifrost., http., url., session., service., k8s., langfuse., openinference., otel.), are skipped. Default false.

headers.description: Custom headers sent to both the trace and metrics endpoints. Supports env.VAR_NAME prefix for environment variable substitution.

trace_headers.description: Extra headers sent only to the trace endpoint, overlaid on headers (same key wins). Supports env.VAR_NAME prefix.

metrics_headers.description: Extra headers sent only to the metrics endpoint, overlaid on headers (same key wins). Useful when a collector requires a per-signal header, e.g. a Databricks table name. Supports env.VAR_NAME prefix.

tls_ca_cert.description: Path to TLS CA certificate file

insecure.description: Skip TLS verification (ignored if tls_ca_cert is set)

otel_profiles_config.description: OpenTelemetry plugin configuration with one or more export profiles.

routing_fallback.description: A fallback in a routing rule's chain. Either the 'provider/model' string ('provider/' keeps the incoming model), or an object that additionally pins a provider key. A string must start with a provider and a slash: a bare provider name such as 'openai' names no provider and is skipped at request time.

model.description: Fallback model name. Omit to use the incoming request model

provider_key_name.description: Optional provider key name. Resolved to internal key_id at config load time. Requires provider.

key_id.description: Optional provider key ID to pin for this fallback. Not together with provider_key_name.

routing_target.description: A single weighted routing target within a rule. All fields except weight are optional; omitting provider or model means use the incoming request value. Weights across all targets in a rule must sum to 1.

provider.description: Target provider name (e.g., 'openai', 'azure'). Omit to use the incoming request provider

model.description: Target model name. Omit to use the incoming request model

provider_key_name.description: Optional provider key name. Resolved to internal key_id at config load time. Requires provider.

key_id.description: Optional provider key ID to pin for this target. Requires provider. Not together with provider_key_name.

weight.description: Probability weight for this target (must be > 0). All weights in a rule must sum to 1

ttft_timeout_ms.description: Time-to-first-token (TTFT) deadline in milliseconds for streaming requests routed to this target. An attempt that produces no first token in time is cut off and the next fallback runs. The last attempt is never cut off, so the setting only takes effect when fallbacks exist. Omit to disable.

routing_rule.description: Routing rule for dynamic provider/model selection

id.description: Unique routing rule ID. Optional: a rule without an id is matched to the stored rule with the same name, scope and scope_id, and gets a generated ID the first time it is stored, so name must be unique within the scope. A rule with an id is matched by id, so changing the id creates a new rule; with source_of_truth split the old rule stays in the database.

cel_expression.description: CEL (Common Expression Language) expression for rule evaluation

chain_rule.description: If true, re-evaluates routing chain after this rule matches

targets.description: Weighted routing targets. Weights must sum to 1. Omit provider or model to use the incoming request value.

scope.description: Rule scope level. User-scoped rules can be created through the API and UI only: config.json does not support them, and a user-scoped rule in it is dropped at load with a warning.

scope_id.description: ID (not name) of the team, customer or virtual key. Required for non-global scopes; ignored for global. A new rule whose scope_id does not resolve is dropped at load with a warning; an edit that does not resolve keeps the stored rule, if the stored rule's own scope still resolves, and is dropped otherwise.

priority.description: Evaluation order within the rule's scope (scope plus scope_id); lower runs first. Must be unique within that scope, counting disabled rules and rules created in the UI or API. Defaults to 0, so two rules in one scope that both omit priority collide, and at startup Bifrost keeps the first and skips the other with a warning. A rule whose priority is held by a stored rule that config.json does not declare (for example the old row left behind by changing a rule's id) is also skipped with a warning. Give every rule that shares a scope its own priority.

query.description: Visual rule builder state for the management UI (react-querybuilder). Omitted unless exported from the dashboard. Not evaluated at routing runtime (cel_expression is). When present, must include combinator and rules[] so arbitrary metadata cannot be mistaken for builder state.

rules.description: Leaf rules (field, operator, value) and/or nested combinator+rules groups from the query builder.

virtual_key_provider_config.description: Provider configuration for a virtual key

weight.description: Weight for load balancing (null opts out of weighted routing)

allowed_models.description: Allowed models for this provider config. Use ["*"] to allow all models; empty array denies all (deny-by-default). An entry starting with regex: is an RE2 pattern matched case-insensitively against the whole model name.

blacklisted_models.description: Models blocked for this provider config even if matched by allowed_models. Use ["*"] to block all; empty array blocks none. An entry starting with regex: is an RE2 pattern matched case-insensitively against the whole model name.

key_ids.description: Key identifiers allowed for this provider config. Use ["*"] to allow all keys. Semantics depend on version: v2 (default) empty = deny all; v1 empty = allow all. Values are the key IDs.

complexity_tier_boundaries.description: Lexical score thresholds. simple_medium and medium_complex are applied by the complexity analyzer; complex_reasoning is retired and accepted for backward compatibility only.

simple_medium.description: Active lexical boundary applied by the complexity analyzer: a request scoring below this classifies as SIMPLE.

medium_complex.description: Active lexical boundary applied by the complexity analyzer: a request scoring below this classifies as MEDIUM, and at or above it as COMPLEX. Must remain greater than simple_medium when supplied, both for the analyzer and for backward compatibility.

complex_reasoning.description: Retired REASONING-tier boundary. Accepted for backward compatibility but ignored because REASONING is merged into COMPLEX.

complexity_analyzer_keywords.description: User-editable keyword scoring signals. The legacy four-list shape remains accepted for config.json compatibility. When the semantic block is present, the three normalized tier lists may contain at most 750 phrases combined; additive config.json merges are checked against that combined limit.

code_keywords.description: Deprecated legacy field. Values are merged into medium_keywords.

reasoning_keywords.description: Deprecated legacy field. Values are migrated to complex_keywords.

technical_keywords.description: Deprecated legacy field. Values are merged into medium_keywords.

complexity_analyzer_config.description: Runtime configuration for complexity_tier CEL routing with semantic or decision-model classification

classifier.description: Primary complexity classifier: semantic, decision or llm. Defaults to semantic.

allOf.description: The llm classifier answers with the llm block's model, so choosing it needs that block; the loader rejects it otherwise.
Selecting the llm fallback without configuring the classifier it names loads a semantic classifier whose non-answers have nothing to fall back to; the loader rejects it for the same reason.

model_router.description: One model router: an id, a name and a description beside the same settings as complexity_analyzer_config; the model each tier gets; and the routing that decides which requests it takes, after the routing rules.

id.description: Stable router id. `defaults` is reserved: it names the endpoint that serves a new router's defaults.

name.description: Display name, unique across routers. Must contain a non-whitespace character.

classifier.description: Primary complexity classifier: semantic, decision or llm. Defaults to semantic.

targets.description: The model each tier gets. A tier with no target keeps the request's model; weights within a tier sum to 1. Omit to keep the targets set in the dashboard; an empty list clears them.

allOf.description: The llm classifier answers with the llm block's model, so choosing it needs that block; the loader rejects it otherwise.
Selecting the llm fallback without configuring the classifier it names loads a semantic classifier whose non-answers have nothing to fall back to; the loader rejects it for the same reason.
Enabled suggestions capture the semantic classifier's vectors and cluster in its embedding space, so they need it as the primary classifier; the loader rejects them otherwise.
Enabled suggestions need a model: their own provider and model (set together), or else the llm block's.

model_router_target.description: One model for one tier of a model router. Omitting provider or model keeps the request's value.

provider.description: Target provider name (e.g., 'openai', 'azure'). Omit to use the incoming request provider

model.description: Target model name. Omit to use the incoming request model

key_id.description: Optional provider key ID to pin for this target. Requires provider.

weight.description: Probability weight within the tier (must be > 0). All weights in a tier must sum to 1

fallbacks.description: Fallback chain used when this target is chosen. A non-empty list replaces the request's chain; omit it or send [] to keep the chain the routing rules set.

model_router_target.$comment: A blank provider or model is no value: the loader trims both and skips a router whose target then sets neither.

model_router_routing.description: Which requests a model router takes. Routers are tried after the routing rules, on the request as the routing rules left it: narrowest scope first (virtual key, user, team, customer, then global), by priority within a scope, and the first enabled router whose condition holds classifies the request. Omit to keep the routing set in the dashboard; a router created without it starts off, global, after the other global routers.

scope.description: Scope level. User-scoped routing can be set through the API only. Routing whose scope_id does not resolve is skipped at load with a warning.

scope_id.description: ID (not name) of the team, customer or virtual key. Required for non-global scopes; ignored for global.

cel_expression.description: Optional CEL condition over the request as the routing rules left it (model, provider, headers and so on). Empty takes every request in the scope. A condition of model == "<name>" lets apps ask for the router by that model name. It cannot use complexity_tier: the router decides the tier once it takes the request.

priority.description: Order within the scope; lower is tried first. Unique within the scope among model routers, separate from routing rule priorities.

complexity_suggestions_config.description: Phrase suggestions for a semantic model router (the complexity analyzer config makes none). When enabled, a sample of the vectors the semantic classifier already computes for classified requests is kept, under each request's log ID, so suggestions can cluster real traffic in the router's embedding space. Only the vector and routing metadata are stored; request text stays in the logs. Capture requires a top-level vector_store: vectors are written only there, never to the embedded storage the semantic classifier can use, so without one nothing is captured. Captured vectors are deleted with their logs, and an hourly cleanup removes those older than lookback_days or the log retention, whichever is shorter. A vector can therefore outlast that limit until the next cleanup, up to an hour, and longer while the vector store is unavailable, since failed deletes are only retried at later cleanups. Turning suggestions off stops sampling but keeps cleaning up what was captured on the configured lookback_days. Removing or disabling the routing plugin deletes every captured vector.

enabled.description: Capture a sample of classified requests for phrase suggestions; default false. Captured requests are kept in Bifrost's vector store, which must be a shared one (Weaviate, Qdrant, Redis or Pinecone): with Chromem, or no vector store, nothing is captured and suggestion runs are refused. Runs started through the API need this block and a suggestion model (provider and model here, or an llm block), not enabled; with false, suggestions run only on demand, never on the schedule. A run started without a suggestion model is accepted and then fails.

sample_rate.description: Share of classified requests captured; default 0.1.

lookback_days.description: Days of captured traffic suggestions draw on, and how long captured vectors are kept (capped at the log retention, and enforced by the hourly cleanup); default 7.

max_clustered_requests.description: Most captured requests one run clusters; the rest of the lookback window is assigned to the clusters found, so request counts still cover all of it. Default 20000.

min_cluster_requests.description: Smallest cluster, in requests, a suggestion is written for; default 6. A run raises it to 0.1% of the requests in its window when that is larger.

provider.description: Provider of the chat model that writes suggested phrases (only an LLM writes phrases). Set together with model; both omitted take the llm block's model when the config is saved.

model.description: Chat model that writes suggested phrases. Set together with provider; both omitted take the llm block's model when the config is saved.

instructions.description: Replaces the shipped phrase-writing instructions. The fixed output and safety rules are added either way; empty uses the shipped instructions.

complexity_suggestions_tier.description: How each suggestion's tier is decided, after its phrases are written. Omitted: the llm classifier on the phrase model.

classifier.description: llm: a chat model prompted with instructions, the tier definitions, and the router's own phrases as examples. decision: a decision model asked one choice question, with the router's tier definitions and its own phrases as each tier's examples. Shipped default phrases are never used as examples. Omitted: llm.

provider.description: Provider of the tier model. Set together with model; both omitted take the phrase model (llm) or the decision block's model, else the shipped decision model (decision), when the config is saved.

model.description: Tier model. Set together with provider.

prompt.description: llm only: the whole tier prompt (instructions, tier definitions and examples), sent as written followed by the fixed output and safety rules. Empty: generated by each run from the router's tier definitions and its own phrases.

instructions.description: decision only: the choice question's instructions, sent as written. Empty: the shipped instructions.

criteria.description: decision only: each tier's definition, signals and examples, sent as written as that tier's choice. A tier left out is generated from the router (its decision definitions and signals, its own phrases as examples).

complexity_suggestions_schedule.description: When phrase-suggestion runs start: at start_at and every interval after it, the same on every node. Default: daily at 03:00 UTC.

every.description: Interval: hours (1h-23h), days (1d-30d) or weeks (1w-4w), as a fixed duration. Default 1d.

start_at.description: The first run, an RFC 3339 time such as 2026-11-12T03:00:00Z. Runs repeat every interval from it, so it also sets the time of day (in UTC: a daily run moves by an hour of local time across a daylight-saving change). Default 1970-01-01T03:00:00Z.

complexity_session_config.description: Session-aware complexity routing. When enabled and a supported session identity is present, Bifrost retains the highest tier observed across normally sequential turns for 24 hours of inactivity. The configured primary classifier supplies tiers; overlapping requests are best-effort.

enabled.description: Enable monotonic session tier retention; default false.

complexity_semantic_config.description: Embedding-based (semantic) complexity classification settings. Presence of this block enables the semantic classifier. The classifier embeds the analyzer's shared per-tier keyword lists as its exemplars.

provider.description: Provider used to generate embeddings for complexity classification

embedding_model.description: Model used to generate embeddings for complexity classification

timeout.description: Per-request embedding timeout (duration string like '1.5s' or '1500ms', or milliseconds as a number; default: 1500ms). Zero, in either form, means the default. On timeout no complexity tier is published and the request is recorded as 'skipped'.

min_similarity.description: Similarity floor a nearest-exemplar match must clear before its tier is used; a match below it publishes no tier and is recorded as 'skipped' (default: 0, meaning the nearest exemplar always wins however unrelated it is). Compared against the backend's own score: chromem, Qdrant, Pinecone, and Redis report raw cosine similarity, Weaviate reports certainty ((cosine+1)/2), so retune when switching backends.

message_history_count.description: How many of the most recent user messages are combined (oldest first) into the text that gets embedded (default: 1, the latest message only). Higher values let a short follow-up inherit the intent of earlier turns, at the cost of diluting the latest message and embedding more input tokens per request. Only user turns count; system prompts and assistant replies are never embedded.

count_toward_budgets.description: Record classification embedding cost against governance budgets (record-only, never enforced; default: false)

vector_store.description: Where exemplar embeddings are stored: 'embedded' uses the built-in chromem store, 'vector_store' uses the store configured in the top-level vector_store section and falls back to embedded when none is configured (default: embedded)

fallback.description: What answers when semantic classification produces no tier: none (default), the configured llm classifier, or the configured decision model.

complexity_llm_config.description: Chat-completion (LLM) classifier settings. Used as the primary classifier when classifier is 'llm', and as the fallback when complexity_semantic_config.fallback selects 'llm', where it runs only after semantic classification produces no tier. Otherwise the block is kept but not used. Tier names (SIMPLE, MEDIUM, COMPLEX) and the response format are fixed: the gateway always appends a non-editable reinforcement stating them.

provider.description: Provider used to run the classification chat completion

model.description: Chat model asked to name the tier. Every classification it makes waits on one completion from this model, so pick a small, fast one.

timeout.description: Per-request classification timeout (duration string like '2s' or milliseconds as a number; default: 4s). Zero, in either form, means the default. On timeout no complexity tier is published and the request is recorded as 'skipped'.

prompt.description: Replaces the shipped classification guidance (max 4000 characters); empty means the shipped guidance is used. The tier-name and response-format reinforcement is appended by the gateway either way and cannot be edited.

message_history_count.description: How many of the most recent user messages are given to the classifier, oldest first (default: 1, the latest message only). Only user turns count; system prompts and assistant replies are never sent.

count_toward_budgets.description: Record classification completion cost against governance budgets (record-only, never enforced; default: false)

auth_config.description: Authentication configuration. Deprecated: Use governance.auth_config instead.

disable_auth_on_inference.description: Deprecated and ignored. Use client_config.enforce_auth_on_inference instead.

pricing_sync_interval.description: Pricing sync interval in seconds. Default is 24 hours. Minimum is 3600 seconds (1 hour).

live_models_sync_interval.description: How often each provider's list-models response is re-fetched in the background, in seconds. Without this, a model an upstream starts serving after the gateway booted stays invisible until a restart or a key edit. Set to 0 to disable background refresh. Default is 1 hour; minimum when enabled is 60 seconds.

base_url.description: Base URL for the provider (optional, required for Ollama). For Bedrock, only the host is used: it replaces the bedrock-runtime host for all inference, a key's bedrock_key_config.endpoints.runtime still wins over it, and the other Bedrock services keep their per-key endpoints or public hosts. Management API updates accept an origin and optional path, without credentials, query parameters, or fragments.

extra_headers.description: Additional headers to send with requests. A value may be a literal, an env.VAR_NAME reference, or a vault.path reference; references are resolved at load time and only the reference is stored. Literal values are masked in API responses while env/vault references stay visible as references; on update, a masked value sent back under the same header name keeps the stored value, while a masked value under a new or renamed header, or on provider create, is rejected with 400.

default_request_timeout_in_seconds.description: Default request timeout in seconds. For streaming requests this bounds the connection, the request write and the wait for response headers; once headers arrive, stream_idle_timeout_in_seconds governs the body.

enforce_http2.description: Force HTTP/2 on provider connections (relevant for Bedrock and other net/http-based providers)

http2_ping_interval_in_seconds.description: Seconds of stream idle before a client-initiated HTTP/2 keepalive PING (0 = disabled; only when enforce_http2).

insecure_skip_verify.description: Disable TLS certificate verification for provider connections. This bypasses server certificate validation and should be used only as a last resort when a trusted CA chain cannot be configured. Prefer ca_cert_pem for self-signed or private CA deployments.

ca_cert_pem.description: PEM-encoded CA certificate to trust for provider endpoint connections (e.g. self-signed or internal CA). Supports inline PEM or env.VAR_NAME.

stream_idle_timeout_in_seconds.description: Idle timeout per stream chunk in seconds. If no data is received for this many seconds, the stream is closed. Default: 120.

keep_alive_timeout_in_seconds.description: Idle keep-alive for pooled connections, in seconds. Set below the upstream server's keep-alive so Bifrost drops idle connections before the server closes them. Default: 30.

max_conns_per_host.description: Maximum number of TCP connections per provider host. For HTTP/2 (e.g. Bedrock), each connection supports ~100 concurrent streams. Default: 5000.

beta_header_overrides.description: Override default beta header support per provider. For Anthropic-family providers, keys are anthropic-beta prefixes (e.g. 'redact-thinking-'); for TypeSafe-based providers, 'typesafe-danger-zone-images' controls the TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images header sent with image and box requests. Values are true (supported) or false (unsupported). Headers not listed use the built-in defaults.

allow_private_network.description: Allow connections to RFC 1918 private IPs (10.x, 172.16.x, 192.168.x). Enable for providers on a k8s pod network, LAN, or private VPC. Loopback addresses (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1) remain allowed regardless of this setting. Link-local addresses (169.254.x.x) are always blocked.
